scope: read the exact client->server body format from the 2697 source

source.sv_packet_event: seq(4) is read first; for CODOL_Target2697ArchivesActive the qport is omitted and the client is matched by NET_CompareAdr; after Netchan_Process the server reads serverId (1 byte) and messageAcknowledge (4 bytes, & 0x7fffffff)
source.sv_execute_client_message: the decrypted remainder is copied verbatim into decompressMsg (no Huffman for CODOL_SERVER); commands are read with MSG_ReadBits(3): clc_move=0, clc_moveNoDelta=1, clc_clientCommand=2, clc_EOF=3, clc_nop=4
source.sv_user_move: after the 3-bit opcode: cmdCount = MSG_ReadByte(msg) (>=1), then cmdCount usercmds; for CODOL_SERVER the usercmd key is CODOL_UsercmdKey(messageAcknowledge, sv.checksumFeed, reliableCommands[reliableAck&127].command, 32)
source.stale_server_id_branch: if (serverId & 0xff) != (sv_serverid & 0xff) the server logs the stale line and may resend the gamestate; otherwise it requires gamestateSent and then parses commands

implications.our_current_body: serverId(1) + messageAck(4) with no command stream, so SV_ExecuteClientMessage has zero bytes to parse and returns immediately
implications.ack_semantics: messageAcknowledge in the body should be the sequence the client has received from the server (the server's netchan outgoingSequence), not the server-side cl->messageAcknowledge we were echoing
implications.why_state_fell_to_2: the packet was accepted (out collapsed) but carried neither a later ack nor a command, so the dedrun considered the client stalled and dropped it to CS_CONNECTED
